items.title: Pope Leo celebrates Mass at St. Augustine's basilica in Algeria

featured_image.name: ALGERIA-VATICAN-DIPLOMACY

items.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass on Tuesday at the Basilica of St. Augustine in Annaba, Algeria, completing a deeply personal pilgrimage to the land where one of Christianity's most influential thinkers lived and died — and marking the first time a pope has ever set foot in the North African country.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran restores limited internet for businesses after 46-day blackout

featured_image.name: Iran Internet Blackout Eases Slightly as Businesses Face ...

items.description:
Iran has begun restoring a sliver of internet connectivity to select businesses after a nationwide blackout that has now stretched past six weeks, in what observers describe as an attempt to stem mounting economic damage rather than a meaningful loosening of digital controls.

State-backed telecom firms are offering a "pro internet" package that companies can apply for through a formal identity verification process, according to digital rights group ASL19. Applicants must explain why they need connectivity and provide supporting documentation to receive access to online services outside Iran, ASL19 and fellow monitoring group Miaan Group said.[1][2]

items.title: About 250 missing after Rohingya boat capsizes in Andaman Sea

featured_image.name: Hundreds missing after Rohingya boat capsizes in Andaman Sea: UN

items.description:
Around 250 people, including Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals, are feared missing after a Malaysia-bound trawler capsized in the Andaman Sea, the United Nations said on Tuesday in a joint statement by the UNHCR and the International Organization for Migration.[1][2][3]

The vessel departed from Teknaf in southern Bangladesh around April 4 carrying an estimated 250 to 280 men, women, and children before sinking on approximately April 9 "due to heavy winds, rough seas, and overcrowding," according to the UNHCR. Only nine survivors have been found, raising fears that the rest perished at sea.[2][4][5]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to direct negotiations after first talks in over 30 years

featured_image.name: Israel, Lebanon Agree to Launch Direct Talks After 'Productive' Washington Meeting

items.description: Israel and Lebanon on Tuesday agreed to begin direct peace negotiations following what the U.S. State Department called "productive discussions" at the first high-level meeting between the two governments in more than three decades. The agreement, reached after talks hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department in Washington, sets the stage for formal negotiations at "a mutually agreed time and venue," according to a department statement.[1][2]

items.title: OECD warns fuel-tax relief risks repeating 2022 mistakes amid oil crisis

featured_image.name: Crude Oil Prices Jump on Fears of a Wider Conflict in the Middle East

items.description: The ongoing war in the Middle East, which has disrupted roughly a fifth of global oil supply since Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in early March, is fueling a fierce debate over the world's dependence on fossil fuels — even as governments rush to cushion consumers from soaring energy costs.

items.title: Trump says US-Iran talks could resume in Pakistan within 48 hours

featured_image.name: Trump says he believes US is close to reaching a new Iran ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump signaled on Tuesday that diplomatic negotiations with Iran could resume in Pakistan within the next 48 hours, reversing his dismissive tone from just days earlier when he said he did not care whether Tehran returned to the table.

In an interview with the New York Post, Trump told reporters stationed in Islamabad, "You should really remain there, as something might unfold in the next 48 hours, and our interest in visiting is increasing." He praised Pakistan's Army Chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, calling his handling of the negotiations "exceptional" and citing it as a key reason for returning to the Pakistani capital.[1][2][3]

items.title: Europe plans Hormuz shipping mission excluding U.S.

featured_image.name: France to deploy almost a dozen warships and mull Hormuz ...

items.description:
European powers led by France and the United Kingdom are assembling a post-war coalition to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz that would deliberately exclude the United States, Israel, and Iran as "belligerent" parties, according to The Wall Street Journal. French President Emmanuel Macron outlined the plan on Tuesday, calling for an international defensive operation built around nations not involved in the fighting, as the transatlantic rift over the war widens into a concrete institutional split.[1]

The initiative, announced by both Macron and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer on X, envisions a conference "in the coming days" bringing together countries willing to contribute to what Macron described as "a peaceful multinational mission aimed at restoring freedom of navigation in the strait". "This strictly defensive mission, separate from the warring parties to the conflict, is intended to be deployed as soon as circumstances permit," Macron said. European diplomats have indicated that European vessels would not operate under American command.[2][3][4][1]

items.title: Scientists find 6,000 km³ of hidden magma beneath Tuscany

featured_image.name: Super magma reservoirs discovered beneath Tuscany

items.description: Two studies published this month are reshaping scientists' understanding of what lies beneath some of the world's most geologically active regions, with one finding that Yellowstone's magma originates far shallower than long believed and another uncovering a vast hidden magma reservoir beneath the rolling hills of Tuscany.

items.title: New footage shows Artemis II capsule opening after Moon mission splashdown

featured_image.name: NASA's Artemis II crew helped by Navy exiting the capsule in new closeup video

items.description: Four days after splashing down in the Pacific Ocean, newly released footage is offering a closer look at the recovery of NASA's Artemis II crew following their 10-day journey around the Moon — the first crewed lunar mission in more than half a century.

items.title: US, Iran eye new peace talks as Hormuz blockade enforcement falters

featured_image.name: NYT: Confusion grows over US blockade as ships still transit Strait of ...

items.description:
The United States and Iran are in discussions for a second round of face-to-face negotiations after weekend talks in Islamabad ended without a deal, even as a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports took effect Monday and tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz tested both sides' resolve.

A White House representative confirmed Tuesday that negotiations are entering a "potential second phase," though no official timeline has been established, CNBC reported. Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian teams could return to Islamabad as soon as Thursday, though the venue, timing, and delegation details remain undecided, with Geneva also under consideration. The ceasefire is set to expire next week, adding urgency to the diplomatic push.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil dips as Iran war fuels historic shift to renewables

featured_image.name: Iran war: A global energy shock could accelerate a shift to renewables

items.description:
The war in Iran, now in its seventh week, has disrupted roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz and sent energy prices to levels not seen since 2022 — but it has also intensified a global pivot toward renewable power that analysts say could reshape energy markets for decades.

Oil prices dipped below $100 a barrel on Tuesday as Iran's president signaled willingness to end the conflict, according to The New York Times, but remained roughly $35 higher than a year ago. The crisis, triggered by U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28, led to the effective closure of the strait and strikes on at least 23 oil and gas sites across the region.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Saudi Arabia urges US to lift Hormuz blockade as standoff enters second day

featured_image.name: US Navy to blockade Strait of Hormuz 'effective immediately ...

items.description: Saudi Arabia is pressing the United States to pull back its naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, warning that the escalation risks destabilizing the region and triggering Iranian retaliation, according to India Today reporting on Monday. The diplomatic push comes as the U.S. military's blockade entered its second day on Tuesday, with Washington and Tehran locked in a standoff over the world's most important oil chokepoint.[1]

items.title: Ships slip past US blockade of Iran despite CENTCOM's zero-breach claim

featured_image.name: US military threatens to blockade all Iranian ports starting on Monday

items.description:
U.S. Central Command declared Tuesday that no ships successfully breached its naval blockade of Iranian ports during the first 24 hours of enforcement, even as independent maritime data suggested several vessels slipped through the Strait of Hormuz unchallenged.

CENTCOM said in a post on X that more than 10,000 U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force personnel, over a dozen warships, and dozens of aircraft are deployed to enforce the blockade, which took effect at 1400 GMT on Monday. Six merchant vessels complied with orders to turn back toward Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman, the command said. The blockade is being "enforced impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas," CENTCOM stated, while emphasizing that freedom of navigation remains in place for ships transiting to non-Iranian ports.[1][2][3]

items.title: Pakistan pushes for new U.S.-Iran talks as port blockade enters second day

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Three ships pass through Hormuz strait amid US, Iran blocks

items.description: The United States military began enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports on Monday, escalating a six-week-old conflict as diplomatic efforts to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz have so far failed. Vice President JD Vance, who led marathon negotiations with Iran in Islamabad over the weekend, defended the move as a direct response to what he called Iranian "economic terrorism."

items.title: Italy suspends defense deal with Israel in reversal by Meloni

featured_image.name: Meloni's tightrope walk: Can Italy's PM leverage her ...

items.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced on Tuesday that her government has suspended the automatic renewal of its defense cooperation agreement with Israel, a move that came just hours after the deal was set to extend for another five years.

"In view of the current situation, the government has decided to suspend the automatic renewal of the defense agreement with Israel," Meloni said on the sidelines of an event in Verona, according to Italian news agency ANSA.[1][2]

items.title: Pope Leo XIV presses on in Algeria after twin suicide bombings rock first day of visit

featured_image.name: ALGERIA-VATICAN-RELIGION-DIPLOMACY-POPE

items.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived Tuesday in the Algerian city of Annaba to walk in the footsteps of St. Augustine, pressing ahead with his historic pilgrimage even as twin suicide bombings on the first day of his visit cast a shadow over the trip.

items.title: Von der Leyen calls for ending EU foreign policy vetoes after Orbán's defeat

featured_image.name: Ursula von der Leyen: the rapid rise of the President of the ...

items.description:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen moved swiftly on Monday to capitalize on Viktor Orbán's stunning electoral defeat in Hungary, calling on EU member states to abandon the unanimity requirement in foreign policy and shift to qualified majority voting — a change that would strip any single country of the power to block decisions on sanctions and military aid.[1][2]

Speaking at a press conference in Brussels, von der Leyen described the move as essential to prevent "systematic blockades" of the kind Hungary imposed during Orbán's 16-year rule, when Budapest repeatedly vetoed Ukraine aid packages and Russia sanctions. She hailed the victory of Péter Magyar and his center-right Tisza party as "a victory for fundamental freedoms," comparing it to Hungary's 1956 anti-Soviet uprising and its 1989 break from communism.[3][1]

items.title: Xi warns of world 'crumbling into disarray' as Spain PM seeks China's help on Iran

featured_image.name: China celebrates Pedro Sánchez

items.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on Tuesday, pressing China to use its diplomatic weight to help end the war between the United States and Israel against Iran and defuse the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. Sánchez told Xi he could think of "few better interlocutors" than China to resolve the situation, according to The Diplomat in Spain, as the two leaders pledged to deepen ties and defend multilateralism against what Xi called a world "crumbling into disarray".[1][2]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon hold first direct talks in decades

featured_image.name: Rubio to join Israel-Lebanon talks at US State Department

items.description: Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors are meeting in Washington on Tuesday for the first direct diplomatic talks between the two countries in over three decades, a session hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department. The meeting, while historic in scope, faces deep divisions over its core objectives — with Israel demanding Hezbollah's disarmament and Lebanon pressing for an immediate ceasefire in a war that has killed more than 2,000 people since early March.

items.title: US blockades Iranian ports as both sides eye fresh talks before ceasefire expires

featured_image.name: How the US Navy could blockade Iran's ports and sweep mines ...

items.description: The United States military began enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports on Monday, a dramatic escalation even as Washington and Tehran explore a possible return to the negotiating table with one week remaining before a fragile ceasefire expires on April 21.
